what: posc: Probability of Outcome Superiority Curves
title: posc: Probability of Outcome Superiority Curves
text: correlation tells strongly predictor outcome related, means decision. probability outcome superiority curve (POSC) answers concrete question: person scores Δ points higher person B predictor, probability also higher outcome? \[P(\Delta) = P(Y_A > Y_B \mid X_A - X_B = \Delta)\] example: one applicant scores 15 points higher another cognitive ability test, likely also perform better job?

title: posc: Probability of Outcome Superiority Curves
code: library(posc)  # From a correlation; differences in raw IQ points (SD = 15) iq <- posc_uni(r = 0.5, n = 200, sd_x = 15,                predictor_name = "IQ", outcome_name = "job performance") iq plot(iq)  # Probability at specific differences, with confidence intervals predict(iq, delta = c(5, 15, 30))  # Directly from data, without assuming normality set.seed(1) x <- rnorm(300) y <- exp(0.8 * x + rnorm(300, sd = 0.6))   # skewed outcome emp <- posc_emp(x, y)                       # 1000 bootstrap resamples (~30 s) plot(emp)                                  # curve and 95% band plot(emp, bins = TRUE, reference = TRUE)   # + binned observed proportions with                                            #   family-wise CIs, and the                                            #   normal-theory curve (dashed) posc_bins(emp)     # the binned proportions as a table plot(posc_emp(x, y, bins = 15), bins = TRUE)  # finer bins  # Compare curves posc_comp(`r = .5` = posc_uni(0.5, n = 100),           `r = .3` = posc_uni(0.3, n = 100)) |> plot()

title: Compare probability of outcome superiority curves — posc_comp
text: bivariate normality POSC determined entirely correlation, curves independent samples can compared testing whether correlations equal. two curves usual Fisher-\(z\) test, $$z = \frac{\tanh^{-1} r_1 - \tanh^{-1} r_2}              {\sqrt{1/(n_1 - 3) + 1/(n_2 - 3)}};$$ two homogeneity test \(Q = \sum_i (n_i - 3)(z_i - \bar z)^2\), referred \(\chi^2\) distribution one fewer degrees freedom curves, \(\bar z\) weighted mean \(z_i\). tests assume curves come independent samples. curves posc_emp() test compares Pearson correlations, shapes curves. test reported curve lacks sample size.

title: Empirical POSC from raw data — posc_emp
text: Pairwise data. Every pair people \((, j)\) \(x_i \ne x_j\) contributes difference \(\Delta_{ij} = x_i - x_j\) indicator whether person higher predictor score also higher outcome (ties outcome count 1/2). large samples random subset max_pairs pairs used. Model. curve modelled $$\mathrm{logit}\, P(\Delta) = \mathrm{sign}(\Delta)\, g(|\Delta|),$$ \(g\) natural cubic spline df degrees freedom intercept, whose basis zero \(|\Delta| = 0\). builds two properties every POSC must , \(P(0) = 0.5\) \(P(-\Delta) = 1 - P(\Delta)\), leaving shape free. 0/1 responses shrunk 0.0005 towards 0.5 fit exists even near-perfect relationships; changes curve negligible amount. Increase df flexible curve; df = 1 makes logit curve linear \(\Delta\). natural spline zero curvature boundary, curve smooth \(\Delta = 0\). forced monotone. Confidence band. Pairs share person independent, model-based standard errors pairwise regression far small. Instead, people resampled replacement n_boot times, curve refitted resample (knots held fixed), band formed pointwise percentiles bootstrap curves. Pairs formed person duplicate excluded. Use set.seed() beforehand reproducible results. Binned observed proportions. check fitted curve data, pairs \(|\Delta| \le\) max_delta grouped bins \(|\Delta|\) observed proportion pairs person higher predictor also higher outcome computed bin. plot(fit, bins = TRUE) shows points whiskers, posc_bins() returns table. whiskers simultaneous (family-wise) confidence intervals: probability level cover bin proportions . computed person-level bootstrap curve, empirical-logit scale \(\ell_k = \mathrm{logit}\{(n_k \hat p_k + 0.5)/(n_k + 1)\}\) bin \(n_k\) pairs: interval \(\mathrm{logit}^{-1}(\ell_k \pm c\,\widehat{se}_k)\), \(\widehat{se}_k\) bootstrap standard error \(\ell_k\) \(c\) level quantile \(\max_k |\ell^*_k - \ell_k| / \widehat{se}_k\) bootstrap resamples (max-\(t\) sup-\(t\) method). intervals therefore asymmetric lie 0 1. Non-monotone relationships. POSC averages predictor's distribution pair people sits. U-shaped relationship, person higher predictor likely higher outcome one side minimum less likely , curve reflects balance two. symmetric U centred middle predictor's distribution true POSC flat 0.5, even though predictor strongly related outcome. empirical curve constrained monotone recovers shapes; dashed normal-theory reference, depends linear correlation, meaningful case.

title: posc 0.2.0
text: posc_emp() estimates POSC directly raw data, normality assumption: spline logistic regression pairwise differences (random subset max_pairs large samples), set P(0) = 0.5 P(-delta) = 1 - P(delta), person-level bootstrap confidence band. posc_emp() also computes observed proportions bins difference (bins = number equal-count bins vector breakpoints). plot() draws points simultaneous (family-wise) confidence intervals, computed max-t bootstrap empirical-logit scale asymmetric stay within [0, 1]. posc_bins() returns table. plot(x, mark = ...) highlights chosen differences: guide line runs x-axis curve, probability labelled (add mark_ci = TRUE confidence interval). Works single curves comparisons. posc_uni(), posc_multi(), posc_lm() posc_emp() return "posc" object print(), summary(), plot(), autoplot(), predict() .data.frame() methods. predict() gives probabilities confidence intervals difference. plot(x, full = TRUE) draws full sigmoid negative positive differences. posc_comp() accepts number curves (named labels) uses homogeneity test correlations two. posc_multi() posc_lm() gain adjust, uses adjusted multiple correlation default correct optimism -sample R. Redesigned plots: default just curve confidence band, axis lines, light gridlines probability axis steps 0.1. Options add percentages (percent = TRUE), remove gridlines (grid = FALSE), automatic title subtitle (title = TRUE, subtitle = TRUE), empirical curves binned proportions (bins = TRUE) normal-theory curve (reference = TRUE). Comparisons use colour-blind-safe palette.
